instruction: Review the 2023 book reading spreadsheet on your desktop. Identify which book had the fastest reading rate (highest words per day). Write this book's title in the 'book_list_result.docx' document.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the book with the highest reading rate (words per day). Verified with Python: Books sorted by words/day descending are The Shining (24767.17), Fire and Blood (4797.59), Brave New World (4217.47), etc. The Shining has the highest reading rate at 24767.17 words/day. Evaluator checks if the DOCX contains 'The Shining'.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: Extracts all text content from DOCX file using python-docx library, handles file retrieval from VM, returns empty string on error
Metric logic is correct: Properly checks if expected text is present in document content using substring matching with case-insensitive default
Parameter handling is correct: Metric function correctly accesses expected.get('text') - when expected.type='rule', get_rule returns config['rules'] directly as {'text': 'The Shining'}
Expected value is semantically correct: 'The Shining' matches the metadata verification showing it has the highest reading rate (24767.17 words/day)
Postconfig is appropriate: Activates Writer window and saves document with Ctrl+S before reading, ensuring file state is fresh
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts text from saved DOCX → Metric checks for presence of book title → Returns 1.0 if found, 0.0 otherwise
Edge case handling: Getter handles missing/empty files gracefully, metric handles non-string results and missing expected text
